parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is a post-coup security state in which the state itself is the principal threat. Section 35(c) is a universal exposure for trans visitors: detention up to three months for being 'suspicious' after sunset, documented as used specifically against transgender people, alongside documented stripping, beating and sexual assault by police. Section 377 remains in active use with life-term penalties and is described as intensified since 2021. Custody brings documented torture and sexual violence; courts and complaints offer no realistic remedy (50% of surveyed LGBT respondents report no legal-system confidence). Killings are documented but lack denominators. A tolerant 2020 public-opinion poll and the nat kadaw tradition do not offset an unremedied hostile state apparatus.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender recognition; state does not recognise trans identity. Passport/ID mismatch with presentation invites scrutiny under section 377 and section 35(c) 'cannot satisfactorily account' reasoning.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No documented acceptance of foreign X markers or mismatched documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch feeds directly into police detention powers exercised under militarised post-coup policing.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Section 35(c) permits detention up to 3 months for suspicious behaviour after sunset, used specifically against trans people. Documented arrest, stripping, beating, 14-day detention; torture and sexual violence in detention post-2021; section 377 carries life imprisonment.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No effective remedy; arbitrary detention and failing courts.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A night-time stop escalates into custody where documented abuse occurs and no oversight functions.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Militarised policing, arbitrary detention and vague public-decency provisions in military-controlled areas documented as endangering the right to life; police are perpetrators of stripping and sexual assault.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility and custody exposure is run by the same apparatus committing the documented abuses; opposition governance does not operate these facilities.

care_services.exposure: 2022 Gender Policy includes LGBTQ people only as a planning-category 'vulnerable group'; no enforceable care right. HIV stigma documented; advocate charged under section 377 in 2018.
care_services.protection: Symbolic policy language only; no enforceable protection.
care_services.interaction: Seeking care risks disclosure to providers operating without anti-discrimination obligations in a collapsed oversight environment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Section 377 intensification post-coup as aggravating factor; police use 'shadow law' specifically against trans people; police called forced naked parade a 'public service'; books banned as 'obscene' in 2025; Emergency Provisions morality clause.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: None enforceable; 2019 Child Rights clause and 2020 broadcasting guidelines are non-binding.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing licenses police extortion, sexual assault and arbitrary detention with impunity.

minors_guardians.exposure: Conscription Law 2024 drives queer people into fear and displacement; vague public-decency and morality provisions expose accompanying families; section 372 and 469 provisions cited as usable.
minors_guardians.protection: 2019 Child Rights Law non-discrimination clause referencing sexual orientation — but child-only and lacking enforcement mechanisms.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family shares the parent regime's detention and documentation exposure; the only child-specific protection is unenforced paper.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented police harassment, sexual assault including rape, extortion. Killings of LGBT people since 2021 (5–12 or 17+2 counts, no denominators, magnitude above background unresolved). 2024 survey: 50% no confidence in legal system, 68% fear repercussions.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2020 poll: 74% favour legality, 81% equal treatment; nat kadaw cultural respect; 2019 suicide inquiry suspended three staff.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public tolerance exists but the post-coup security forces operate without accountability, so societal acceptance confers no practical protection once stopped.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No enforceable anti-discrimination law; no LGR; arbitrary detention documented; international organisation's March 2026 verdict is 'avoid entirely'. Section 377 charges beyond 2018 and current section 35(c) frequency are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National human rights commission calls for anti-discrimination provisions (not enacted); opposition government records LGBT killings (does not govern).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns all point the same direction — thin or absent recourse beneath an actively hostile enforcement regime.

anchor_checks.comparison: Very similar: a morality/public-decency statute in active use, custody measured in weeks-to-months with documented beatings and stripping, and courts that do not function for trans complainants. Lower than this dossier only because 0.15-A adds an unused capital clause and systemic coerced confessions; here the analogous gap is the absence of any denominator for killings.

Higher than this dossier. 0.25-C's worst features are birth-sex prison placement, a cross-dressing statute, slow remedies and brief sentences; it lacks this dossier's documented torture and sexual violence in detention, three-month 'shadow law' custody, life-term statute and post-coup killings. This case sits a full step below on the precedence ladder.

Lower than this dossier's comparator tier but still illustrative: 0.35-B involves hours-long identity checks and releases without charge under a functioning courts regime. Here detention reaches three months under statute with documented custodial abuse and no functioning remedy, so 0.35 understates severity materially.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is state-perpetrated: a criminal statute with life-term exposure, a police-act clause permitting three-month detention used specifically against trans people, and post-coup documentation of torture, sexual violence and killings, all beneath institutions that do not remedy complaints. This is precedence-ladder tier 2 (state-tolerated/directed targeting) bordering tier 1, with a universal night-time exposure every trans visitor carries. The dossier's genuine positives — a tolerant 2020 poll, nat kadaw visibility, symbolic policies — describe society, not the security apparatus the traveller meets when outed, and rule-of-law failure means they cannot mediate. Killings lack denominators and are weighted as unresolved; the rating rests on documented custody abuse, the shadow law and absent recourse.
